analysis.title: Energy, Utilities & Mining Pulse: Investors Asking: What Are the Impacts of Recent Elections on Natural Resources Equities?
key_insights: Per GS, the S&P 500 and XLE traded -2% and -8% from Monday to Friday after Tuesday's US elections. The note asks each team which stocks could draw incremental investor interest or pushback after the results.

Utilities (Davenport): Democratic wins raise near-term uncertainty on data center development, especially in Texas and Georgia, where both governors-elect have mentioned temporary moratoriums. GS calls it largely a timing issue and not a demand issue. The Texas result surprised investors most and drove the largest moves in VST, NRG, CEG, SRE and AEP. TLN fell 8.5% on Wednesday despite no Texas exposure.

GS sees incremental interest in defensive regulated utilities with limited exposure to data-center-sensitive markets (DUK, ES, AEE, ED), and in renewables-exposed NEE. It sees more limited interest in defending the IPPs, and still finds TLN attractive with no Texas exposure.

Clean tech (Lee): a Democratic House could reduce the perceived risk of further legislative tightening after OBBBA, particularly for higher policy beta names (ENPH, RUN, ARRY, SHLS, FSLR, NXT). GS argues stocks price less risk of tightening but assign little value to possible restoration of curtailed credits. 45X is a particularly meaningful earnings driver for FSLR because of its US manufacturing footprint.

GS expects FSLR and NXT/ARRY/SHLS to draw the most incremental interest. ENPH and RUN could face pushback because the positive election read-through offsets a weak residential backdrop of elevated rates and softer demand.

Midstream (Mackay/Foster): two compounding impacts preceded a broad sell-off. Data center timelines changed the gas demand growth outlook, and administration commentary on the Middle East coincided with a significant decline in oil and LNG prices. Names exposed to power and gas demand (WMB, DTM, KMI, KGS) fell as investors reassessed project backlogs and pre-FID spend priced into valuations.

Midstream: GS says post-FID projects should support growth even if FID timelines extend. TRP highlighted at least a 5% CAGR to 2031 EBITDA on sanctioned projects alone. GS sees a window for behind-the-meter solutions to take share and keeps its view that Permian growth stays supported above $65-70/bbl WTI. EE was a bright spot after strong earnings.

Energy services (Petrick Breno/Mehta): Specialty Contractors fell over 20% on average since market open on Nov 4 on fears of slower or delayed data center builds. GS calls the sell-off overdone for PWR and MTZ, where data centers are a smaller share of earnings than traditional transmission and distribution work, and sees risk/reward skewed to the upside.

E&P (Mehta): after the election, focus shifted to Middle East dynamics as oil futures fell. Week over week the 2027 Brent strip is down 5% and spot crude is down 15%. XOP traded -15% over the past week against XLE -12% and the S&P 500 -3%.

GS values oily E&Ps on a mid-cycle deck of ~$73/$68 Brent/WTI against a strip averaging $84/$79 for 2027/2028. On that conservative deck, the coverage trades at an average 14% FCF yield on 2027/2028 estimates. Exhibit 2 is described as E&Ps reflecting a cost of capital well above 11%.

Select E&Ps signalled higher 2027 capital spending, namely MUR and APA. APA reported 3Q26 beats versus consensus on EBITDA and production and guided a ~$2.50bn 2027 program against ~$2.10bn at the 2026 guidance midpoint. MUR's Bubale prospect in Cote d'Ivoire screened as positive, with 2-4 appraisal wells at $80-$110 mn each. APA and MUR (+1%/+4%) outperformed XOP (-1%) after Wednesday post-market results.

Integrated oils (Mehta/Petrick Breno): the Middle East risk premium, which had inflated to the high $20s, is unwinding rapidly. Global crude benchmarks fell roughly 8-9% on Wednesday and 15-16% on the week, leaving Brent below $100, while physical crude flows in the Middle East are back near pre-war levels. Majors left activity, capex and shareholder return guidance unchanged.

GS prefers CVX over XOM on free cash flow growth. At $75/b Brent, GS estimates a 2028 free cash yield of 8% for CVX versus 6% for XOM. Data center policy risk to Project Kilby is seen as a small part of the portfolio.

Metals and mining (Cash): the election does not change current Section 232 tariffs absent formal policy action. Democrats are pushing for more Congressional oversight of tariff authority, which affects the medium to long-term backdrop. GS says the near-term steel debate stays on domestic supply/demand, imports and pricing, plus capital discipline and shareholder returns.

FCX: the board approved the $4.5bn Bagdad expansion. It roughly doubles mining and milling rates, lifts long-term output to ~400mn lbs copper and >20mn lbs moly, and cuts unit net cash costs by ~20%. GS sees it as a positive marker for execution. Investor sentiment stays cautious on a possible data center slowdown, lower global growth, cost inflation and a potential 2027 copper tariff.

FANG/VNOM: investors cite strong FANG 3Q26 oil production and raised oil guidance, the outsized gas production, the Barnett update and M&A outlook. VNOM announced $889 mn of incremental transactions, and the more cautious investors want clarity on large-scale M&A and on FANG's preferred ownership level of VNOM.

PR: investors focus on strong 3Q26 results and $1.15 bn of announced acquisitions, including ~$1.03 bn for Ridge Runner Resources II, adding ~13 Mboe/d. Cautious investors question inventory depth and continued M&A at higher oil prices.

Refining: debate centres on whether elevated freight rates persist. VLO management said a VLCC voyage from the Gulf Coast to Asia now costs ~$30-$35/bbl versus ~$5/bbl in 2025. Investors see wider light-heavy differentials as supportive for VLO, MPC, PBF, PSX and DINO, and value PSX's 40 time-chartered ships.

Canadian oils: strong CFPS beats and solid downstream earnings. CNQ reached C$13 bn net debt, which unlocks 100% of free cash flow to shareholders, under a new C$800 mn monthly buyback pace. WTI-WCS widening is attributed by management to freight rates, not pipeline egress, and investors watch Canadian trilateral MOU updates into November 15.

Energy services: Behind-the-meter investors worry that ESA and PPA announcements get pushed out by data center regulation uncertainty and focus on financing. They are waiting for ESAs before turning constructive. Oilfield services conversations centre on regional exposure, with companies pointing to mid to high single digit international growth in 2027 ex-Middle East.

Compression: AROC reported its strongest bookings since 2Q23 on rising Permian gas-to-oil ratios, viewed favorably for KGS, which reports 3Q26 next week. USAC and AROC both flagged lubricant cost headwinds, with USAC's exit run-rate ~25% above 1H26.

MPLX/MPC: management said on the MPLX 3Q26 call that it would always look at the structure and intends to renew the contract ahead of its early-2028 expiry. Investors ask whether ~$12b of parent-level cash at MPC and the YTD share price divergence create a framework for a transaction, with a taxable event for MPC as a possible limit.

Utilities earnings: investors were constructive on 3Q capital plan and EPS growth increases from AEP, WEC and XEL, while FE is debated on transmission and West Virginia upside. Investors are more negative on SRE, SO and AEP because of Texas and Georgia exposure. Most investors do not expect clarity on Texas until mid 2027 and show no appetite to add IPPs (VST, NRG, CEG) at current levels.

Solar: interest rose after the post-midterm rally, and investors ask whether it reflects short covering and positioning or a durable re-rating. FSLR demand and pricing remain debated while investors await the first deals priced under the updated Section 232 framework. FLNC announced CEO and CFO transitions, and investors ask about permanent appointments and execution on its $6.4bn backlog.

earnings_insights: APA 3Q26 (reported, with results on Wednesday after the close): strong beats versus consensus on EBITDA and production. 2027 capital program guided at ~$2.50 bn versus a 2026 guidance midpoint of ~$2.10 bn.
MUR 3Q26 (reported Wednesday after the close): signalled higher 2027 capital spending. Management commentary implies 2-4 incremental appraisal wells on Bubale at $80-$110 mn per well.

FANG 3Q26 (reported Nov 2 after the close): strong oil production, raised oil production guidance and outsized gas production. VNOM announced $889 mn of incremental transactions alongside its release.

PR 3Q26 (reported): strong results and $1.15 bn of announced acquisitions in the quarter, including ~$1.03 bn for Ridge Runner Resources II, adding ~13 Mboe/d. Management guides a ~$35/bbl breakeven on that deal.

Canadian oils 3Q (reported this week): strong CFPS beats, solid downstream earnings and significant shareholder returns. CNQ hit C$13 bn net debt with a C$800 mn monthly buyback pace. SU kept free funds flow and break-even targets intact.
Majors 3Q (reported): management teams left activity, capital spend and shareholder return guidance unchanged. GS estimates 2028 free cash yield at $75/b Brent of 8% for CVX versus 6% for XOM.

Refiners 3Q (reported): VLO management said a Gulf Coast to Asia VLCC voyage now costs ~$30-$35/bbl versus ~$5/bbl in 2025. Investors debate whether freight keeps pressuring light-heavy differentials.
AROC 3Q (reported): strongest bookings since 2Q23, driven by rising Permian gas-to-oil ratios. USAC cited exit-3Q lubricant cost run-rates ~25% above 1H26. KGS 3Q26 is expected next week.

EE (reported strong earnings this week): GS calls it a structural beneficiary of lower LNG prices and Middle East de-escalation. TRP highlighted at least a 5% CAGR to 2031 EBITDA on sanctioned projects.
Regulated utilities 3Q (reported): capital plan and EPS growth outlook increases from AEP, WEC and XEL. FE communicated transmission spend upside and West Virginia opportunity.
SHLS 3Q26 (reported): beat-and-raise with FY26 outlook raised. ARRY lowered guidance but reported a record order book. FSLR 3Q results left demand and pricing as key debates.

FLNC announced CEO and CFO transitions with an operational update. METC lowered FY26 volumes and raised costs, with stronger 2027 pricing and sales as an offset. VLTO beat in 3Q26 and raised its FY2026 outlook.
FCX (announced Nov 4 pre-market): board approved the $4.5bn Bagdad expansion, which the company expects to roughly double mining and milling rates.
